categories.name: DevOps Foundations

roles: Junior DevOps Engineer (where entry-level experience is accepted)
careerFocus.reality: These are targets, not guarantees. Apply when you can demonstrate the required skills and explain your projects. Application-support experience is relevant but is not automatically DevOps engineering experience.

projects.title: Project F1 — Linux Operations Toolkit
tasks: Create a Linux VM or safe lab environment.
Write Bash scripts to check disk, memory, processes and service status.
Log results and use useful exit codes.
Document usage and troubleshooting.

projects.title: Project F2 — Containerised Application + CI
tasks: Choose a small Python, Node.js or static web application.
Store source in GitHub and use a basic branch workflow.
Create a Dockerfile and run the application.
Use GitHub Actions to run checks and build the image.

projects.title: Project F3 — First AWS Deployment
tasks: Deploy a small application to EC2 or another suitable low-cost AWS service.
Configure IAM access and network rules.
Configure the app to start reliably and inspect logs.
Add basic health monitoring and cleanup instructions.

categories.objective: Understand the systems, tools and workflows DevOps engineers use daily. Learn each topic to a practical working level, practise, then move forward without trying to master advanced details immediately.
exitCriteria: Use Linux to inspect processes, services, permissions, disk and logs.
Explain IP addresses, DNS, ports, HTTP/HTTPS, SSH and basic firewall behaviour.
Use Git branches, commits, merges and pull requests.
Write small Bash scripts and basic Python automation.
Build and run a Dockerised application.
Create a basic CI/CD pipeline and explain each stage.
Deploy a simple application to AWS with sensible access and network controls.
Explain monitoring, secrets handling and basic incident troubleshooting.

categories.name: Linux Troubleshooting & Automation

topics.title: Bash Error Handling and Robust Scripts

careerFocus.reality: Target roles whose experience requirements match your profile. Be ready to demonstrate hands-on ownership of pipelines, infrastructure and deployments. Kubernetes/cloud specialist roles may need deeper experience.

projects.title: Project I1 — End-to-End CI/CD Delivery
tasks: Build a pipeline with checkout, tests, build, image scan and publishing.
Deploy to a test environment after successful checks.
Separate configuration from code and protect secrets.
Add deployment verification and rollback.

projects.title: Project I2 — AWS Infrastructure as Code
tasks: Use Terraform to create a small, secured AWS environment.
Use variables, outputs, modules and remote state concepts.
Use Ansible or cloud-init for repeatable configuration.
Demonstrate plan, apply, change review and cleanup.

projects.title: Project I3 — Kubernetes Deployment and Observability
tasks: Deploy a containerised app to local Kubernetes or a cost-controlled managed cluster.
Configure Deployments, Services, probes, ConfigMaps and Secrets appropriately.
Create Prometheus/Grafana dashboards or equivalent monitoring.
Cause a test failure and document diagnosis and recovery.

categories.objective: Connect tools into repeatable workflows. Automate infrastructure and deployments, operate container workloads, add observability and troubleshoot realistic failures.
exitCriteria: Build CI/CD with tests, image publishing, deployment and rollback.
Provision AWS infrastructure using Terraform and understand remote state.
Automate host configuration with Ansible.
Deploy with Docker Compose and understand Kubernetes basics.
Deploy workloads to Kubernetes using Deployments, Services and configuration.
Create metrics, dashboards and alerts.
Use secret management and vulnerability scanning in a delivery workflow.
Troubleshoot build, deployment, connectivity, permission and runtime failures.

topics.title: AWS Load Balancing and Auto Scaling
AWS S3, RDS and Managed Services

categories.name: Production Linux, Automation & CI/CD

roles: DevSecOps Engineer with deeper security expertise
Senior DevOps Engineer after relevant professional experience
careerFocus.reality: This stage builds toward experienced and specialist roles. Completing lessons alone does not qualify someone as senior; employers expect production ownership, judgment and incident experience.
careerFocus.aiops: AIOps / Intelligent Operations specialisation, typically after building solid DevOps, cloud, and observability skills.

projects.title: Project A1 — Production-Style Platform
tasks: Deploy a multi-service application with separated environments and repeatable infrastructure.
Use Terraform modules and CI/CD or GitOps with review gates.
Add ingress/load balancing, health checks, resource limits and access controls.
Document architecture, threat considerations and cost.

projects.title: Project A2 — SRE, Monitoring and Incident Simulation
tasks: Define a service-level objective and measurable indicators.
Create useful dashboards and alerts.
Simulate an outage, diagnose telemetry, restore service and write a blameless postmortem.
Practise backup restoration and recovery objectives.

projects.title: Project A3 — Secure GitOps Kubernetes Platform
tasks: Use Argo CD or another GitOps controller for reviewed changes.
Package workloads with Helm and environment-specific configuration.
Add scanning, secret handling, least-privilege access and policy checks.
Demonstrate failed deployment, rollback and recovery.

projects.name: AIOps Incident Intelligence Lab
projects.description: Build a lab that collects metrics and logs, detects abnormal behaviour, groups noisy alerts, suggests evidence-based root causes, and proposes remediation. Require human approval before actions that change infrastructure.

categories.objective: Design, secure, scale and recover production systems. Advanced topics require practice and judgment; not every employer or role uses every listed tool. Add an AIOps specialisation applying statistics, anomaly detection, event correlation, incident investigation, and carefully controlled AI assistance to observable systems.
exitCriteria: Design resilient deployments and explain availability, recovery, security and cost trade-offs.
Operate Kubernetes with resource controls, autoscaling, access controls and troubleshooting.
Use GitOps to promote reviewed changes.
Design reusable Terraform modules and safe state/change workflows.
Create SLOs/SLIs, alerts, dashboards and incident runbooks.
Apply supply-chain security, scanning, secret controls and policy checks.
Demonstrate disaster recovery, backup restoration, rollback and post-incident learning.
Explain architecture decisions, risks, costs and capacity trade-offs.
Demonstrate an AIOps lab with documented evaluation, false-positive handling, evidence-backed incident summaries, and human-approved remediation; explain the limitations of AI-generated diagnoses.
